### Problem

The engine cannot tell whether a change to the AI improves or worsens the flow, neither for DiluxOne nor for an organisation that adopts it, so the same failures come back and each one costs a person's time and a paid run.

### Scope

The evaluation sets per step and their runner (generalising `scripts/review-eval.py` and `review-eval.yml`), the layering through the configuration overlay and the packs, the cases from private repositories by reference, proposing new cases from the flow's failures, the gate on AI changes and on releases, the quality numbers, and the docs that describe them (docs/model.md, docs/testing-and-quality.md, docs/adopting.md, kinds/README.md).

### Out of scope

The "Test first" check for code (#734). The release lane's test identity (#727). Choosing or changing models.

### Acceptance criteria

C1: Given each of the six AI steps, when its set is listed, then it has real cases from the history with an expected outcome, and a deterministic grade wherever one is possible.
C2: Given a pull request that changes a step's prompt, model or AI policy, when its checks run, then that step's set runs and the pull request fails if its score is worse than the step's baseline.
C3: Given a release candidate of the engine, when the release runs, then every step's set runs and the tag does not move if any score is worse than its baseline.
C4: Given a person stepping in (`needs-human`, a manual unblock, a bug that comes back), when the flow records it, then it proposes the case to that step's set.
C5: Given an organisation that adopts the workflows and has `evals/` in its `.github`, when a set runs for its repositories, then its cases are added to the engine's and the kind's, scored against its own baseline, and nothing specific to DiluxOne is hard-wired.
C6: Given a case from a private repository, when it is stored and run, then the set holds only its reference and expected outcome, it runs in that organisation's runners with its token, and only the score is written.
C7: Given the weekly numbers, when they are published, then they show per step and per repository the share merged with no person stepping in, the bugs that came back, the manual unblocks and the avoidable questions.
C8: Given docs/model.md, docs/testing-and-quality.md, docs/adopting.md and kinds/README.md, when a reader looks for how the AI is measured and how an organisation adds its own cases, then they say it.

### Criticality

Normal
